People ask me whether cows were happier in Rosi's day, with about four thousand kilos, or today, with eight to ten thousand. The honest answer: that depends on the farmer more than on the number. Rosi had a good one – my father.

Whenever a student says “only” eight thousand kilos, I think of Rosi. About four thousand kilos per lactation, and we were proud of every one of them. Eight to ten thousand today is an achievement. So was Rosi's.

Rosi stood in a tie stall, like all thirty cows on our farm – that was normal back then. She gave about four thousand kilos a lactation. Today's cows give eight to ten thousand, and many of them can move about freely. Both deserve our respect.
